q: How does Chapter 1 primarily characterize the move from chat interfaces to persistent agents?
options: A capability shift driven by larger models
A hosting shift from cloud to on-premises
A temporal shift: the agent operates continuously across time
A pricing shift from per-seat to per-token billing
explanation: The book argues the change is mainly about time: an agent's state carries forward, while a chat exchange is complete in itself. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.1)

q: An operator reviews logs on Friday and finds the agent acted all week on a wrong assumption it recorded on Monday. Which risk category is this?
options: Compounding errors
Permission escalation chain
Operational costs without feedback
Output channel failure
explanation: A wrong decision written to memory keeps shaping later behavior, which the book calls compounding errors. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.1)

q: Which of the following was NOT part of the combination that let OpenClaw spread?
options: Single-file configuration in openclaw.json
Self-hosted deployment on commodity hardware
Multi-channel communication over real messaging platforms
A proprietary fine-tuned model
explanation: OpenClaw's edge was integrating existing parts; the model capability was already available to earlier systems. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.1.1)

q: According to Chapter 1, what was wrong with the conventional system prompt approach?
options: It used more tokens than identity files
It was opaque, brittle, and reset every session
It could not be combined with tool calling
It required a vector database
explanation: The book describes system prompts as hidden from users, fragile under unexpected input, and non-persistent. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.2)

q: A team must process thousands of structured form submissions per day with exactly-once guarantees and minimal cost per run. What fits best?
options: A Claw-pattern agent on a frontier model
A Claw-pattern agent with heartbeats disabled
A workflow automation tool such as n8n or Zapier
A RAG system over the submissions
explanation: Deterministic, high-volume, structured work with strict execution guarantees is where workflow tools beat agents. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.2.1)

q: Which Claw subsystem is the first access-control checkpoint, discarding unauthorized events before they use model resources?
options: Context construction
Event intake
Tool execution
Output channels
explanation: Event intake normalizes inputs and drops unauthorized events before any model call. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.3)

q: Compared with a RAG system, how does the book describe Claw-pattern memory?
options: Retrieved by semantic similarity from a vector store
Filled by a separate ingestion pipeline
Loaded as small fragments on demand
Written by the agent as dated narrative logs, with identity files loaded in full
explanation: Claw memory is narrative, agent-authored, and includes identity files that are always fully loaded. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.3.1)

q: A user says "keep my inbox organized." By Wednesday the agent has archived promotions, created folders, and unsubscribed from newsletters. Which mitigation does the book map to this risk?
options: Explicit permission design and hard limits in SOUL.md
Routing to a cheaper model tier
Enabling prompt caching
Lengthening the heartbeat interval
explanation: This is scope expansion, which the book's risk table pairs with permission design and SOUL.md hard limits. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.4)

q: How does the book characterize the February 2026 inbox deletion incident?
options: A hallucination bug in the email tool
A predictable result of a capable system lacking specified intent, scope, and reversibility
A supply chain attack through a malicious skill
A provider outage that duplicated delete calls
explanation: The agent did not malfunction; default delete access, no confirmation gate, and a broad instruction combined. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.4)

q: In the first month of a new deployment, what is the main activity of week 3?
options: Connecting the first real data source
Writing the initial identity files
Calibrating autonomy based on observed behavior
Analyzing the first operational incident
explanation: By week 3 the operator has enough observed behavior to tune where the agent is too cautious or too aggressive. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §1.4.1)
